subject: Renewal sequencing & burst allowance — Navitus mid-quarter expansion
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Amy Li <amy.li@navitus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal sequencing & burst allowance — Navitus mid-quarter expansion

Hi Amy,

Congrats again on the pilot metrics — the model latency and inference throughput numbers you shared look excellent. Per our conversation this morning, I put together a short proposal for handling the expected spike in Q3 while keeping the renewal simple. High level:

- Option A (Preferred): Add a 90-day "burst bucket" of 1M generation tokens at a blended uplift rate (15% higher than your committed unit price) that draws from dedicated capacity. We auto-bill on consumption; any unused burst tokens expire at the end of the 90-day window.
- Option B: Temporary committed top-up for 3 months (50% additional commit) with pro-rated billing and a step-down to your existing commit after month 3. This reduces unit price but requires a short-term invoice adjustment.

Both options can be written as a small amendment to your existing renewal so it co-executes with the annual contract but does not force a full re-quote. I attached a draft SOW and a one-page summary of the two options.

Ask: can you confirm which option Procurement would prefer, and whether Navitus needs an SLA credit line included in the amendment? If you want, I can loop in Priyom to produce a clean DocuSign amendment and PO-ready SOW.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
(415) 555-0193

Attachments: Navitus_SOW_v3.pdf (draft), pricing_workbook_navitus_q3.xlsx (calc)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Li <amy.li@navitus.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sequencing & burst allowance — Navitus mid-quarter expansion

On Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Amy,
>
> Congrats again on the pilot metrics...

Thanks Mina — quick notes from an SE perspective:

- Burst bucket sizing: 1M tokens seems reasonable given their peak reports, but we should include a soft alert threshold at 600k tokens so Navitus can trigger a provisioning decision earlier.
- Blended uplift calculation: propose 1.15x committed unit price for burst consumption; if they convert >70% of the burst into committed capacity within 60 days, offer a conversion credit equal to 25% of the uplift paid.
- SLA: standard 99.9% serving SLA applies; for the amendment we can add a 0.5% monthly credit for sustained infra incidents >2 hours that impact their production path.

I'll sketch the math in the pricing workbook and mark the line items. Priyom, can you confirm whether the conversion credit is okay from renewals/SAM standpoint?

- Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Amy Li <amy.li@navitus.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@navitus.ai
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sequencing & burst allowance — Navitus mid-quarter expansion

Thanks Mina (and Ben),

This looks promising. Procurement wants the normal PO + clean SOW flow. A couple of questions:

1) Can you produce a one-page amendment that lists the burst bucket as a charge line and the conversion credit logic? Procurement prefers deterministic invoicing lines rather than ad-hoc credits.
2) Is the SLA credit wording something you can standardize so our legal team doesn't have to redline heavily?
3) If we pick Option A, will we get immediate capacity (i.e., true burst) or do we need a lead time? We need to know if this is usable within 48 hours.

We can commit to the burst bucket quickly if the DocuSign flow is clean. I'll also ask finance to pre-approve a short PO for the uplift amount so we can speed execution.

Amy Li
Head of Platform, Navitus Health
amy.li@navitus.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Amy Li <amy.li@navitus.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 16:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Revised pricing structure & DocuSign-ready amendment

Hi Amy, Mina, Ben —

Thanks for the quick turn. I updated the workbook and drafted a one-page amendment that reflects Option A with deterministic invoicing lines. Summary of changes:

- Burst bucket: 1,000,000 generation tokens billed at $0.00115/token (15% uplift over committed $0.001/token); line item shows total uplift amount.
- Conversion credit: if Navitus converts >= 70% of burst tokens into committed capacity within 60 days, apply a credit equal to 25% of the uplift amount; the credit posts on the first full invoice after conversion.
- SLA credit: standardized language: "If monthly downtime attributable to Redwood's serving layer exceeds 0.1% for the Customer's production route, Customer is eligible for a credit equal to 0.5% of monthly fees for each 0.1% increment of downtime, up to 2% per month." Legal-friendly and consistent with existing templates.
- Lead time: for Option A we guarantee capacity allocation within 24 hours for burst buckets tied to Dedicated pools; if the customer is on Private deployment additional network approvals may add time (not applicable here).

I've attached the draft amendment (DocuSign template ready) and the updated pricing_workbook_navitus_q3.xlsx with line-by-line math. Please review and tell me if Procurement needs any specific PO language for the invoice description.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Attachments: Navitus_SOW_v3.pdf (amendment v1), pricing_workbook_navitus_q3.xlsx (revised)

Priyom / Mina —

Thanks for the fast turn. Procurement and Finance gave verbal approval this morning for Option A with the conversion credit. Attached is our PO (Navitus_PO_4587.pdf).

A few operational asks before we sign:
- Please ensure the DocuSign amendment calls out the exact invoice line: "Q3 Burst Bucket — Navitus Health — 1,000,000 tokens" so our accounts payable matches it to the PO.
- We need the SLA language put into the amendment exactly as you shared; Legal will do a quick scan but won't redline if it matches the template.
- Please expedite the Dedicated pool allocation; we want the capacity available by EOB tomorrow (Aug 5).

If you can get the DocuSign link and the final amendment today, I'll route for signature.

Best,
